title: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
summary: On the morning of 1 November 1755, All Saints' Day, a major earthquake with an Atlantic epicentre struck Lisbon. Fires and a tsunami followed, and Lisbon was devastated. Damage spread across Portugal's coast and North Africa. The disaster spurred the beginnings of modern seismology and sharp debate among Enlightenment writers.

uncertainty.note: Day is consistent across both sources; time of day given only as about 9:30 a.m. by one source.

where.modern_name: Lisbon, Portugal (pin is the city centre, a proxy; the epicentre lay offshore in the Atlantic, about 200 km southwest per Earth magazine)

importance.justification: Destroyed a European capital, triggered a tsunami across the Atlantic region, and helped start modern seismology.

audience_note: Describes a disaster with large loss of life, fire and drowning.

sources.title: Lisbon Earthquake
sources.publisher: Rachel Carson Center, LMU Munich (Environment & Society Portal)

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on magnitude (8.7 vs 8.5) and I left it out; the pin is Lisbon city, not the offshore epicentre. Only two non-coordinate publishers.
